name: Mika
cost: Free (Apache 2.0). You pay your model provider for the API key you bring
works_with: Android phones, with any model that supports tool calling; also reachable from AI tools on your computer over MCP
short: An Android app that takes a one-sentence request and does it on your phone: working your apps, browsing the web and running scripts.
what: Mika drives apps on a hidden background screen while you keep using your phone. It reads the screen and taps and types like a person, so apps don't need special support. It also has a built-in browser, a local Linux sandbox for Python, Node and shell, scheduled tasks and a memory. There is no Mika server: your requests go only to the model provider you set up.
who: Android users who want an agent that actually does things in their apps. It's an early public beta, mostly tested on one Android 14 phone, and many demos and built-in app notes cover apps popular in China.
needs: Android 11 or later for chat, web and sandbox tasks. Android 12 or later to control apps, and Android 14 or later recommended
An arm64 phone for the Linux sandbox
An API key for a model that supports tool calling, or a ChatGPT Plus or Pro sign-in
Developer options and wireless debugging turned on for app control (paired once)

steps.title: Install the APK
steps.text: Download the latest APK from the repo's Releases page (https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest) and install it.

steps.title: Skip accessibility for now
steps.text: Mika turns accessibility on by itself after pairing. Android often blocks turning it on by hand for apps from GitHub, so choose Skip when the wizard reaches it.

steps.title: Pair wireless debugging once
steps.text: Open "Set up phone control" in Settings. Turn on Developer options, USB debugging and Wireless debugging, then pair with the 6-digit code. Skip this if you only want web, files and chat.

steps.title: Add a model
steps.text: In Settings, open "Models", pick a preset or Custom, enter your API key and tap "Test and save". Or tap "Continue with ChatGPT" to sign in instead. The main model must support tool calling.

steps.title: Optional: use it from your computer
steps.text: With the phone on USB, this turns on computer access and prints a URL and token for your AI tool's MCP config. It only works over the cable.
steps.code:
adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/connect-computer.sh
adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Check the weather at 8 every morning and tell me only if it will rain", or "Set alarms for 9:40, 9:50 and 10:00 tomorrow morning".

watch: In the default Ask mode, only steps that spend money are confirmed. Sending messages, posting, submitting forms, deleting and changing settings just happen. Autonomous mode doesn't even ask before paying.
Automating third-party apps and websites may break their terms of service and risks restricted features or account bans. The README says to use it at your own risk.
What you say, screen contents and screenshots go to the model provider you choose. Keys and memories are encrypted on the phone.
It needs wireless debugging and accessibility, which give it deep control of your phone.
Batch jobs, like greeting several recruiters, start without asking you to confirm the list first.
